text:
In ring-closing metathesis of an octa-1,7-diene, the terminal \( \ce{CH2} \) groups are expelled as ethylene, and C2 and C7 form the new cyclic double bond:

\[
\ce{CH2=CH-C3-C4-C5-C6-CH=CH2
->[RCM]
cyclohexene + CH2=CH2}
\]

To place methyl groups at C3 and C4 and an isopropyl group at C5 of the cyclohexene, the precursor must be:

\[
\ce{CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH(CH3)-CH(iPr)-CH2-CH=CH2}
\]

This is 5-isopropyl-3,4-dimethylocta-1,7-diene. (Option C is the same connectivity numbered from the opposite end; A uses the preferred lower locant set \(3,4,5\).)

Answer: A
